messages.subject_clean: how to compile and adapt cran packages
messages.body_plain:
Hi Georg,
You can actually just put together a pom.xml file that specifies paths
matching GNU R's typical layout, see for example:
http://nexus.bedatadriven.com/content/groups/public/org/renjin/cran/bootstrap/2012.04-0-SNAPSHOT/bootstrap-2012.04-0-20130708.165947-1.pom

The goal is to be able to use CRAN packages without modification, but
in practice, not (yet) all C and Fortran code compile completely
through our toolchain, and packages using S4 generally don't work at
all at this point.

We're *almost* done with the automated tool chain, where you may find
a build of the package you need:
http://renjinci.appspot.com/packages

(There still some work left to be done -- but the package search
should work already)

messages.subject: Re: how to compile and adapt cran packages
messages.subject_clean: how to compile and adapt cran packages
messages.body_plain:
Hi Georg,

I've submitted a pull request to your github repo with an updated pom that tells maven to use GNU R's directory layout: basically that R sources are in ./R instead of /src/main/R and that C/Fortran sources are in ./src rather than the default ./src/main/c and ./src/main/fortran

I've also added two missing implementations of C functions in the latest build of Renjin that were needed by forecast's C code: https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/commit/797a1eab4b7327e8d5c7592ab457e0b98c16fea6

If you run `mvn clean install` now, you should get the following error:

```
[ERROR] Failed to execute goal org.renjin:renjin-maven-plugin:0.7.1537:gnur-sources-compile (gnur-compile) on project forecast: Compilation of GNU R sources failed: Exception translating function calct: Exception thrown while translating call null = gimple_call <&cdivid, T3501, T3499, hvr.66, hvi.65, &tr, &ti>: null.tr <http://null.tr> [PrimitiveFieldExpr] is not addressable -> [Help 1]
```

Which is a problem with Renjin's C compiler: it should be detecting when global variables (which get translated as Java fields) need to be addressable because there are pointers to them, but it's not so compilation fails. I'll try to take a look at this week. I'm taking a second pass at the gcc-bridge code because it's become a bit dense.

As MJ said, I haven't even looked at C++ code yet, and Renjin won't try to compile it at the moment, but I don't consider beyond the realm of possiblity. GCC does all of the hard work of compiling the C++ for us, so we should be able to use the same toolchain that compiles C and Fortran because we'd be getting the same input.

If you run:
mvn3 clean install -Dignore.gnur.compilation.failure=true

Then the package does get built and you can load in Renjin using:

library(com.github.geoHeil.forecast)

Of course methods that rely on native code will fail.

I'm playing around with the native code compiler this week, I'll use this as a test case to see how far we can go.

On Wednesday, July 1, 2015 at 4:17:42 PM UTC+2, Maarten-Jan Kallen wrote:
> I would say that the presence of C++ code is at least one problem, but there may be others (like missing dependencies). Renjin will not support C++ code so ideally this code is translated into Java (not C).​ It looks like the package also has a lot of dependencies related to graphics so we would need to strip those out as well.
>
> Maarten-Jan

Regards

Maarten-Jan
